ai_summary: Great Britain’s wind fleet is currently generating 16.6 GW, with Scotland providing an estimated 5.6 GW, operating at 55.4% of installed Scottish wind capacity. This strong renewable output has driven Scottish carbon intensity to an impressive 0 gCO2/kWh, standing in stark contrast to 72 gCO2/kWh GB-wide. However, acute transmission bottlenecks across the Anglo-Scottish border continue to restrict power flow south to major demand centres. Consequently, 14.2 GWh of Scottish generation has been curtailed so far today through Balancing Mechanism bids, creating a constraint cost of about £784,733. To replace this trapped zero-carbon volume, fossil plants elsewhere were instructed to burn an estimated 2,704,460 m3 of gas, needlessly generating 4,982 tonnes of CO2 emissions. Extrapolating today’s constraint expenditure across a full year indicates an estimated total yearly cost of £286 million. When distributed across national electricity consumption, this recurring transmission friction adds an estimated £1/MWh to every consumer’s invoice in the UK. Unlocking this stranded clean energy through strategic grid reinforcement remains essential to eliminating fossil backup and driving down nationwide system costs.
